column1: # Planted scan roots for check/kernel_dispatch.sh scalar-f32: the exit code and the line it names.
# Columns, tab-separated, none empty ("-" for none): fixture (a directory beside this
# table), args (gate arguments, "{}" is the fixture path), stream (both, out or err: the
# gate's output the needles are read from), exit (exact), has (strings that must all
# appear), lacks (strings none of which may appear), is (the whole output; "\t" is a
# tab), what (what the case proves). Needles are fixed strings separated by ";;".
# In has, "A;>B" is one needle: B must appear after the first A.
# The gate flags a scalar_f32( call that nothing casts back to the operand dtype: an f32
# scalar combined with a bf16 activation promotes the result to f32. A call passes with a
# non-F32 .astype( on its own line or on a continuation line of the same chain, or with a
# f32-ok marker on its own line or in the comment block directly above; a cast whose
# target is F32 keeps the f32 and is no guard. A row that must fail names the file and
# the line of the call, so a gate that fails for another reason does not count as recall,
# and a row that must pass names the number of files it scanned, which is what makes an
# excluded directory visible: a violation planted there passes only if it was left out.
# The refusals (nothing to scan, a missing root, --min, a bad option) exit 2 and print

column8: a scalar_f32( cast to the operand dtype on the same line passes
a bare scalar_f32( with no cast is caught

an F32 cast on a continuation line does not resolve the chain
a chain still open at the end of the file is reported, not dropped
a cast on the line after a finished statement does not guard the earlier call
a same-line f32-ok marker exempts the call
an f32-ok marker on the comment line above exempts the call
a marker in the first line of a multi-line comment block directly above still applies
a blank line between the marker and the call ends the comment block
a marker does not survive a plain statement between it and the call
one marker exempts one call, not the call on the next line
